probes.question: What does the law of large numbers say about repeated random events?
options: Their average tends toward the expected value
Every outcome becomes equally likely next time

probes.question: True or false: a casino must win every single spin to make a predictable profit.

image.alt: Ornate facade of the Monte Carlo Casino with arched windows, marble columns and colourful mosaic frieze.

body.claim: A casino can lose on one spin of the roulette wheel, yet reliably profits over many.
body.why: This is the law of large numbers. The average of many repeated random results moves toward the expected value, so the casino's earnings tend toward a predictable percentage. A player's winning streak is eventually overwhelmed by the odds built into the game.
